newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress says support for government conditional.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress says support for government conditional.

text.p: The new chief of India's Congress party warned on Thursday that the party's crucial support for the ruling centre-left coalition depended on reciprocal backing for Congress in India's most populous state.

"I must say that when I support them at the centre (federal government), I would like to get the same treatment in Uttar Pradesh to block the BJP," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Sitarm Kesri as saying.
"If they do not consider this then we will have to think," he said. His warning was not "election rhetoric", he said.
The Congress teamed up with the ruling United Front alliance in June to keep out the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) because of its perceived bias against India's minority Moslems.

Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state, is holding critical state elections over three days scheduled to end on October 7. The poll is widely seen as a test for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition.
The BJP emerged in May as the largest single group in the Indian parliament after general elections but its 12-day-old government resigned as others closed ranks to form a majority.

Kesri, a veteran independence fighter, took over the Congress last month as a stopgap chief after the exit of former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, who resigned as president following a court summons in a criminal conspiracy case.

In another sign of what newspapers described as an effort to consolidate his hold over India's oldest political party, the United News of India (UNI) said on Thursday that Kesri had postponed an expected party election.

UNI quoted a Congress party statement saying that a new party chief would be elected on March 12. Party officials had earlier said that the party's plenary would meet to elect a new president some time after the Uttar Pradesh elections.
Rao served as prime minister from 1991 until last May when his party finished a humiliating second in general elections.
